_note: The referee's thresholds (spec 9.1): where the rulebook relies on a human referee's eye. 'values' is what the rules engine loads; 'docs' gives each value's unit, source and note. Rule numbers are the WPBSA Official Rules of Snooker, 2024-25.

touching_gap_m.source: Section 3 Rule 8 (touching ball), Section 2 Rule 18 (spot occupied); the value is ours
touching_gap_m.note: Balls the simulator leaves in contact rest within a nanometre of touching; 0.05 mm is far below what a referee can see and above any rounding. The opening rack's seeded gaps (0.01 to 0.1 mm) only separate reds from reds, which this never asks about.

simultaneous_hit_s.source: Section 3 Rule 6; the value is ours
simultaneous_hit_s.note: The simulator resolves contacts one at a time, so only contacts at the same instant count as one impact: the guide line then tells the player truthfully which ball is hit first. Equal to the simulator's zero_time_s.

push_contact_time_s.source: Section 2 Rule 19; Alciatore, 'The Illustrated Principles of Pool and Billiards', high-speed video HSV A.76 and technical proof TP A.9: a tip stays on the ball for about 0.001 s
push_contact_time_s.note: A first contact with an object ball sooner than this after the strike is a push: the tip would still be on the cue ball. The simulator's strike takes no time, so a cue ball leaving at 2 m/s reaches a ball 2 mm away in this time. 0 turns the test off (a touching ball that moves is still reported).

push_fine_edge_rad.source: Section 2 Rule 19(b): no push when the cue ball hits a very fine edge of an almost touching ball; the value (80 degrees) is ours
push_fine_edge_rad.note: The cut at the moment of contact (the angle between the cue ball's direction and the line of centres towards the object ball) from which the contact is a very fine edge. With several balls met at once, one contact thicker than this makes the push.

miss_lenient_gap_m.source: Section 3 Rule 14(a); the owner chose the television standard on 2026-11-15
miss_lenient_gap_m.note: With no clear path to a ball on, a failed attempt whose cue ball passed within this of one is a foul only. 0 calls every failed escape a miss, as professional referees do.

escape_max_cushions.source: Section 3 Rule 14(a)(ii); the value is ours
escape_max_cushions.note: The ball on is impossible to hit when no route with at most this many cushions reaches any part of it. Routes with more cushions exist on a real table but nobody is expected to find them.

pot_attempt_radius_m.source: ours; the same distance the shot cycle uses for a ball played at a pocket (ShotCycle.attempt)
pot_attempt_radius_m.note: A stroke counts as an attempt to pot when the first ball hit was potted or passed within this of a pocket's drop circle. Only the frame summary's pot success uses it.

stalemate_quiet_travel_m.source: Section 3 Rule 17 ('the situation remains basically unchanged'); spec 9.1 leaves the thresholds to the builder
stalemate_quiet_travel_m.note: A stroke is quiet when nothing is potted and the object balls end, summed over all of them, less than this from where they began.

stalemate_offer_strokes.note: Quiet strokes in a row, by both players together, before a re-rack is offered.

stalemate_grace_strokes.source: Section 3 Rule 17(a): 'usually after three more strokes to each side'
stalemate_grace_strokes.note: After an objection the frame is re-racked when this many more strokes are all quiet.

d_sample_step_m.source: Section 2 Rule 17(a): snookered in hand means from all possible positions in the D; ours
d_sample_step_m.note: The D is tested at points this far apart, its edge included.
